stories.headline: Trump defends Iran deal as White House unveils details In a sprawling news conference at the G-7 summit in France, the president touted the economic benefits of the ceasefire and threatened force if it fails.
stories.summary: President Donald Trump defended the Iran deal at the G-7 summit in France, touting its economic benefits and warning of force if it fails. He claimed that oil reserves would have run out in four weeks if the Strait of Hormuz had not been reopened, leading to "bedlam." The deal, which extends a shaky ceasefire, has received support from other G7 leaders, with French President Emmanuel Macron calling it a "very good deal" that puts a stop to instability with terrible economic consequences. Trump hailed the deal as "historic" and threatened force if it fails, while also criticizing his predecessors, Barack Obama and Joe Biden. The International Energy Agency has warned of declining oil reserves and exceeding demand this year, adding context to Trump's remarks on oil reserves.

stories.headline: Trump signs Iran peace plan, claiming deal averts ‘worldwide depression’ President says 14-point agreement with Tehran has delivered a ‘major win’ for the United States
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump has signed a 14-point peace agreement with Iran, claiming it averts a "worldwide depression" and is a "major win" for the United States. Iran's president, Masoud Pezeshkian, also signed the agreement from Tehran. The deal is expected to be formally signed by US Vice-President JD Vance in Geneva on Friday. Trump stated that the agreement helps end the war and achieves his goal of ending Tehran's nuclear ambitions. Iran had previously confirmed plans to end hostilities, and the agreement is seen as a significant development in US-Iran relations. The signing of the deal marks a shift from earlier threats of renewed military action against Iran, with Trump now predicting a quick end to the conflict. The agreement's details and implications are expected to be further clarified in the coming days.

stories.headline: Congress jabs govt. over Iran-U.S. MoU signing, calls it severe setback to PM's foreign policy Congress criticizes the government for the Iran-U.S. MoU, calling it a setback to PM Modi's foreign policy and regional influence.
stories.summary: The Indian Congress has criticized the government over the recent Iran-US Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), calling it a severe setback to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's foreign policy. The MoU, also referred to as the 'Islamabad MoU', has sparked controversy, with Congress leader Jairam Ramesh slamming it as a blow to India's regional influence. This comes after the US and Iran exchanged strikes, prompting India to call for a peaceful resolution. Despite initial concerns, Prime Minister Modi had welcomed the emerging US-Iran peace agreement, hoping it would restore peace. However, the Congress has now come out strongly against the government, citing the MoU as a failure of Modi's foreign policy. The development has significant implications for India's relations with the US, Iran, and the broader region. The Congress criticism highlights the complexities of India's foreign policy in the face of shifting global dynamics.

stories.headline: Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Frank-Walter Steinmeier launch car assembly plant in Tashkent News and analytical articles about Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan.
stories.summary: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier have launched a car assembly plant in Tashkent. This development comes as Mirziyoyev continues to engage in diplomatic efforts, having visited multiple countries in his first 10 months in office, including Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Russia, China, and the US. He has also met with various world leaders, showcasing Uzbekistan's growing international presence. Recently, Mirziyoyev presented Uzbekistan's economic performance, highlighting a $4.2 billion critical minerals program aimed at transforming the country's mining industry into higher-value production. The program is a key part of Uzbekistan's industrial policy, seeking to leverage its Soviet-era mining strengths for modern supply chains. The car assembly plant launch demonstrates the country's efforts to attract investment and boost its economy.

stories.headline: Apple prepares second-generation iPhone Air for early 2027
stories.summary: Apple Inc. is preparing a second-generation iPhone Air for early 2027, aiming to boost the appeal of the slimmed-down device. According to people with knowledge of the matter, the new iPhone Air is expected to launch in spring 2027. This development comes as the company also plans to introduce its first foldable smartphone later this year. Additionally, Apple is working on a 20th anniversary iPhone for 2027, featuring a curved screen that wraps around the device's edges. The second-generation iPhone Air is part of Apple's efforts to enhance its product lineup and attract more customers. The exact features and specifications of the new iPhone Air have not been disclosed, but the launch is anticipated to take place in early 2027, with some reports suggesting a spring release.

stories.headline: Samsung Redefines Everyday Wellness With Connected Care Solutions at VivaTech 2026
stories.summary: Samsung Electronics is showcasing its vision for AI-powered connected care at VivaTech 2026, held at Paris Expo Porte de Versailles from June 17 to 20. The company's interactive exhibit and panel discussion demonstrate how an open partner ecosystem drives healthcare innovation. Samsung's connected care solutions aim to redefine everyday wellness, leveraging artificial intelligence to improve healthcare outcomes. The exhibit highlights the company's collaboration with partners, including Google, to develop innovative healthcare solutions. Samsung's AI-powered connected care vision is part of its broader efforts to integrate technology into daily life, enhancing overall well-being. The showcase at VivaTech 2026 provides a platform for Samsung to share its vision with industry leaders, innovators, and attendees.

stories.headline: Windows Search will stop searching your embarrassing typos on Bing
stories.summary: Microsoft is updating Windows Search to improve its ability to find apps with typos, dropped letters, or partial words. Previously, Windows Search would default to Bing web results for mistyped queries, potentially leading to embarrassing searches. The new update allows Windows Search to suggest installed apps even with incorrect or incomplete input. A new toggle will also be available to disable web search in the main search function, forcing local-only search and stopping Store and web results. This change is currently available in the latest Windows 11 Insider preview build and is expected to roll out to all users soon. The update aims to reduce unnecessary Bing usage and provide a more seamless search experience for Windows users. The change was first announced at Microsoft's Build conference earlier this month.

stories.headline: MAXHUB Showcases AI-Powered Collaboration and Display Solutions at InfoComm 2026
stories.summary: MAXHUB is showcasing its AI-powered collaboration and display solutions at InfoComm 2026. The company is demonstrating its AI Meeting Experience on the XBoard V7, highlighting how AI can simplify hybrid collaboration through intelligent features. MAXHUB's latest innovations in AI-powered collaboration and professional display solutions are on display, including smart collaboration tools, AI-powered meeting experiences, and integrated commercial display solutions. As a global leader in integrated communication displays and unified communications solutions, MAXHUB is leveraging InfoComm 2026 to explore the transformation of modern workplaces through AI, AV, and integrated technologies. The event showcases MAXHUB's commitment to delivering cutting-edge solutions for connected and intelligent work environments. Attendees can experience MAXHUB's latest offerings, including its Windows-based Microsoft Teams solutions, at the conference.

stories.headline: Israel Folau flames ‘double standards’, wife Maria video Wests Tigers talks He was told he could be back in the NRL for the rest of this season. Now the chance of representing the Tigers is gone.
stories.summary: Israel Folau's potential return to the NRL with the Wests Tigers has been scrapped. Folau's wife, Maria, revealed on Instagram that Wests Tigers' Benji Marshall had initially expressed interest in having Folau join the team for the remainder of the season. However, the opportunity was later withdrawn due to anticipated media distractions and disagreements from certain board members. Folau's camp claims an ARL Commission member intervened to block his comeback. Folau has spoken out against the decision, citing double standards in the NRL's treatment of players with controversial pasts. He expressed frustration that his Christian beliefs were deemed a problem, while players who have committed offenses have been allowed to return to the game. Folau's bid to return to the NRL after a 16-year absence has ultimately been unsuccessful.

stories.headline: Fifa responds to reports of fans getting into England v Croatia without a ticket Reports said scores of fans had breached security and entered AT&T Stadium without any sort of check
stories.summary: FIFA has responded to reports of fans entering the England v Croatia World Cup match without tickets, stating they are unaware of any such incidents. Reports had emerged citing eyewitnesses claiming scores of fans had breached security and entered AT&T Stadium in Dallas without being checked. However, FIFA has played down these reports, rejecting claims that ticketless England supporters managed to enter the stadium. The organization has stated that they are currently unaware of any supporters gaining entry to the match without valid tickets. FIFA's response comes after concerns were raised about security at the stadium during the World Cup 2026 opener. The incident is still being monitored, but FIFA maintains that they have no evidence of fans entering the stadium without tickets.

stories.headline: Thomas Tuchel slams Fifa for ruining his 'very special moment' just before England kicked off World Cup campaign THOMAS TUCHEL snapped at Fifa after photographers ruined his “very, very special moment” when God Save The King was played before England’s...
stories.summary: Thomas Tuchel, England's national football team coach, criticized FIFA after photographers blocked his view of his team during the national anthem, "God Save the King," before England's World Cup campaign kickoff. Tuchel described the moment as "very, very special" but said it was ruined by the presence of 50 photographers standing half a meter away, preventing him from seeing his players. Despite the pre-match frustration, England delivered a strong performance, winning 4-2 against Croatia. Tuchel expressed his emotional attachment to the occasion, stating it was a dream come true, and requested FIFA to consider moving photographers to allow coaches to fully experience the national anthems. FIFA has been contacted for comment on the matter. Tuchel's team went on to have a successful match, with a notable second-half surge.

stories.headline: Under the radar: These less-than-stars have made an impact at the World Cup While the biggest names in soccer are getting the most attention at the World Cup, the expanded tournament also has provided some unheralded players with moment
stories.summary: Several unheralded players have made an impact at the World Cup, alongside global stars. Matthew Garbett, a winger for Scottish club Motherwell, became the first New Zealand player to score two goals in a World Cup game. Egypt's Mohamed Ashour scored his first international goal with an outside-the-box blast against Belgium. Luis Díaz sparked Colombia to a 3-1 win over Uzbekistan with a goal and an assist in his World Cup debut. Other notable performances include Livano Comenencia scoring Curacao's first World Cup goal, Boualem Khoukhi helping Qatar earn a point, and Jovo Lukic netting Canada's first World Cup goal. These players are taking advantage of the expanded tournament to shine on the global stage, earning recognition and accolades in the process. Their performances are adding depth and excitement to the World Cup.

stories.headline: When Hindu majority opposes construction of church near temple, authorities must listen: Madras HC
stories.summary: The Madras High Court has stayed the construction of a church near a Hindu temple in Coimbatore, citing vigorous opposition from the Hindu majority. The court noted that the church was proposed to be built on a public road, which should not have been permitted. The judges stated that when Hindus constitute an overwhelming majority and oppose the construction of a church near a temple, authorities must not brush aside their objections. The court also mentioned that Coimbatore is a communally sensitive city, and the state has a duty to aid in the enforcement of established religious rights. The stay was granted due to potential mala fide intent behind the proposal to build the church near the temple. The court's decision emphasizes the need for authorities to consider the sentiments of the local community.

stories.headline: Dowry abuse, CCTV surveillance: Woman dies by suicide only 47 days into marriage
stories.summary: A 26-year-old woman, Vishakha Tilkar, died by suicide just 47 days into her marriage. Her family has accused her husband, Dr. Nitin Tilkar, and his family of dowry harassment, physical abuse, and constant CCTV surveillance. The victim's family claims she was taunted for not bringing enough cash and jewelry, and was monitored through CCTV cameras installed inside and outside the house. Vishakha was allegedly not allowed to freely speak with her parents or neighbors and was assaulted two days before her death for speaking with a nearby woman. The husband and in-laws have been accused of sustained abuse, which possibly led to her suicide. The incident occurred in Ambernath, and an investigation is underway. Vishakha's family has alleged that the abuse began soon after the marriage, which took place on April 30.

stories.headline: 'Kiss Me Here': Australian Tourist Harassed In Kolkata Streets, Video Viral
stories.summary: An Australian tourist, Marco, was harassed by a young man in Kolkata who repeatedly asked for a kiss on his cheek. The incident occurred on a street in Kolkata, where the young man, sitting in a rickshaw, approached Marco and said "Kiss me here, kiss me." Despite Marco's discomfort, the man continued to make the request. A video of the encounter has gone viral, with Marco stating he felt "molested" by the experience. The incident has sparked online debate about consent, public behavior, and the treatment of foreign visitors in India. The video shows Marco walking along the street when the young man approaches him, making the unwanted advances. The tourist's account of the incident has triggered a widespread discussion on social media platforms.

stories.headline: Toppers, Marksheet & Pass Percentage of CA Final May 2026 Exams
stories.summary: The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) has declared the results for the CA Final May 2026 exams. Noor Singla has secured the All India Rank 1 with a score of 83.17%. The overall pass percentage for both groups is 14.07%. The results include the pass percentage details and the total number of candidates qualifying as Chartered Accountants. ICAI has also published the merit list, which includes the topper list, ranks, and marks. The pass percentage and topper list are available on the ICAI website. A total of candidates have cleared the exam, with details available on the ICAI website. The results were declared on June 18, 2026, and candidates can check their results and the merit list on the official ICAI website. The pass percentage and topper list provide insight into the performance of candidates in the CA Final May 2026 exams.

stories.headline: [Bloomberg] Would Andy Burnham Want the England Job, Too? Who would even want to be the UK’s prime minister? The list of problems is endless: anemic growth; crumbling public services; soaring welfare bills; unhappy geo
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer is facing pressure to resign after a major defeat in local elections. Despite his desire to continue, Starmer's leadership is being questioned by Labour MPs amidst cabinet tensions and ministerial resignations, including Health Secretary Wes Streeting. The UK is dealing with various challenges, such as anemic growth, crumbling public services, and soaring welfare bills. With speculation surrounding possible successors, Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham's route to Westminster is becoming clearer. The country has seen five prime ministers in seven years, with none serving a full parliament, highlighting the instability of British politics. The situation is being closely watched, with some wondering who would want to take on the role of prime minister given the numerous problems the UK is facing.

stories.headline: [The Economic Times] FPIs pump record funds into G-Secs after policy shift Foreign funds are pouring into India's government bond market at a record pace this month, driven by tax exemptions on interest and capital gains, a wider inves
stories.summary: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) are investing in India's government bond market at a record pace this month. The influx is driven by tax exemptions on interest and capital gains, a wider investment basket, and relaxed limits. As a result, FPIs have pumped in Rs 8,795 crore into government securities after the tax exemption. The 10-year benchmark government security yield eased to 6%. The policy measures have improved market sentiment, strengthened the rupee, and increased foreign demand for government bonds. This surge in investment comes after a total outflow of Rs 93,731 crore in 2025. The recent tax reforms and relaxed investment limits have reshaped the investment landscape, attracting global funds to Indian government bonds at a 15-month high. The increased FPI activity is expected to bolster India's bid for global index inclusion.

Google's AI data centers have been showcased, providing insight into the company's operations. stories.headline: Rahul Gandhi's political journey from novice to challenger
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi posted an audio file of his speech at the opposition alliance meeting on June 8 on his YouTube channel. In the speech, he discussed his stance on alliances and relationships with other party leaders. Specifically, he mentioned that he cannot have a close relationship with Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan due to their ongoing political battle in the state. This statement comes as the Congress party has aligned with another party in Tamil Nadu, whose leader had previously expressed hesitation about joining the INDIA bloc. Rahul Gandhi's speech highlights the complexities of his political relationships and alliances within the opposition bloc. The full transcript of his speech is available on his official website and YouTube channel, credited as "Source: Rahul Gandhi's YouTube Channel, @rahulgandhi".

stories.headline: Rahul Gandhi's birthday marks a significant milestone in his career
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi, the Leader of the Opposition, turned 55 on June 19, 2025. Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended warm birthday wishes to him, expressing good wishes for his future. Congress party chief Mallikarjun Kharge also praised Gandhi for his dedication and commitment to the party. The birthday marked a significant milestone in Gandhi's career, with some speculating it could be a launchpad for youth engagement, as evident from the Indian Youth Congress's mega job fair. However, the celebration comes amid the party's continued decline, as seen in the Bihar 2025 elections, where the Congress secured only 6 seats, raising questions about Gandhi's leadership impact. Despite this, Gandhi received birthday wishes from various leaders, acknowledging his presence in Indian politics.

stories.headline: The evolution of Rahul Gandhi as a political leader
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi, an Indian politician and leading figure of the Indian National Congress, has evolved significantly as a political leader. Born on June 19, he is the son of Rajiv Gandhi and grandson of Indira Gandhi. Over the years, he has transformed from a political novice to a primary challenger. His journey has been marked by struggles within the Congress party, particularly regarding the preference for dynasty over merit. Despite this, Rahul Gandhi remains a powerful leader in the party. His interactions and public appearances, including with notable figures like Messi and students, have been closely watched and discussed. As he celebrates his birthday, a recount of his journey highlights his growth and development as a political leader in India. His role in the Congress party continues to be a subject of interest and discussion.

stories.headline: Rahul Gandhi's transformation into a primary challenger in Indian politics
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi, a leading figure of the Indian National Congress, has transformed into a primary challenger in Indian politics. Born on June 19, he is the son of Rajiv Gandhi and grandson of Indira Gandhi. Despite the Congress party facing losses in multiple state elections and major political battles under his active leadership, Rahul Gandhi remains a key figure. The BJP has officially claimed that the Congress has suffered losses during his leadership phase. However, Rahul Gandhi has been vocal about the current political climate in India, expressing his perspective on curbing public dissent. As a prominent politician, his journey from a political novice to a primary challenger is notable, with his party continuing to navigate the complex Indian political landscape.

stories.headline: Stock Markets Today: Sensex, Nifty Pare Early Losses Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty recovered early losses to trade higher, supported by encouraging developments on the geopolitical front, specifically
stories.summary: Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty recovered early losses to trade higher, supported by positive developments on the geopolitical front. The indices had ended marginally higher on Monday, with the Sensex and Nifty touching new highs recently. However, the rupee extended losses for the sixth straight day, ending down by 36 paise. Despite volatility in the equity market, the outlook for Nifty and Sensex remains positive, with bullish momentum expected to drive the Nifty 50. The BSE Sensex had previously fallen 479.26 points to close at 76,009.70, while the NSE Nifty declined 118 points to settle at 23,913.70. Today, the Indian markets are expected to perform positively, driven by encouraging geopolitical developments and overall market trends. The recovery in Sensex and Nifty indicates a strong market sentiment, despite recent fluctuations.

stories.headline: Stock markets end higher for fifth day in a row on lower crude prices, optimism over U.S.-Iran peace deal Stock markets rose for the fifth consecutive day, driven by lower crude prices and optimism over the U.S.-Iran peace deal.
stories.summary: Stock markets have risen for the fifth consecutive day, driven by declining crude prices and optimism over a potential US-Iran peace deal. The rally is fueled by hopes that a peace agreement will be reached, which has led to a drop in oil prices of over 10% and a 7-cent decrease in domestic gas prices per gallon. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 have seen gains of 0.6% and 0.7%, respectively, in anticipation of the deal. Despite a brief pause in the rally after a tentative ceasefire was broken, markets have continued to surge. The potential agreement has eased geopolitical tensions, boosting investor confidence and driving stocks higher. Major US stock indexes have ended the week higher, reflecting cautious optimism around the possible US-Iran agreement and declining oil prices.

stories.headline: Sensex trades flat, Nifty below 24,050 as markets snap gaining streak after Fed’s hawkish signal Indian stock market is trading lower as Sensex and Nifty snap a four-session gaining streak after a hawkish US Federal Reserve tone raised rate hike expectation
stories.summary: Indian stock markets are trading lower, with the Sensex trading flat and Nifty below 24,050. This marks a snap in the four-session gaining streak. The decline is attributed to a hawkish tone from the US Federal Reserve, which has raised expectations of a rate hike. The Indian stock market had been performing well prior to this, but the Fed's signal has led to a reversal. The Sensex and Nifty had been on an upward trend, but are now experiencing a downturn. The market is reacting to the potential rate hike, which could impact investor sentiment and market performance. The Nifty is currently below the 24,050 mark, indicating a significant decline from its previous highs. The market will likely continue to be influenced by global economic trends and monetary policy decisions.

stories.headline: Sensex, Nifty in flux: US Fed throws hot water on West Asia peace deal momentum Stock market update: Crude oil slide keeps bulls in play, but US Fed rate scare pulls down IT stocks
stories.summary: Indian equity benchmarks Sensex and Nifty experienced volatility after an initial rally. The US-Iran peace deal announced by US President Donald Trump boosted investor confidence, causing a sharp rally with the Sensex soaring over 1,100 points and the Nifty nearing 24,000. The decline in crude oil prices, with Brent crude tumbling 2.1% to around $75.9 a barrel, also supported the market. However, the US Fed's potential rate hike scared investors, pulling down IT stocks such as TCS and Infosys. The initial gains were partially offset, with the Nifty and Sensex trading lower after opening in the green. The market is closely watching the developments, with the crude oil slide keeping bulls in play, but the US Fed rate scare posing a challenge. Investor sentiment remains cautious amid the mixed signals.

stories.headline: IMF Raises Alarm As Stablecoin Boom Reshapes Nigeria’s Payments Landscape
stories.summary: Nigeria received approximately $59 billion in crypto-asset inflows between July 2023 and June 2024, ranking second globally. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has raised concerns over the country's stablecoin boom, which has evolved into a major channel for remittances. The IMF warns that stablecoin adoption is testing Nigeria's monetary and regulatory frameworks, posing digital dollarization risks. The fund also flagged payment infrastructure gaps as a factor fueling the stablecoin boom. In its latest report, the IMF urged the Central Bank of Nigeria to sustain monetary policy reforms and address these gaps. Nigeria's plans to raise $5 billion through a Total Return Swap arrangement have also been cautioned by the IMF. The stablecoin boom is reshaping Nigeria's payments landscape, prompting the IMF to call for careful monitoring and regulation.

stories.headline: Rising Inflation Tests CBN Resolve As Analysts See Interest Rates Staying Higher For Longer
stories.summary: Nigeria's inflation rate has dropped to 20.12% as of August, down from previous highs. Despite this decrease, analysts believe interest rates will remain high for longer. The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has held its interest rate at 26.5%, keeping borrowing costs unchanged. The CBN initially increased interest rates to combat high inflation and encourage people to save. Although the inflation rate has declined, it remains high, putting pressure on the economy and living costs. The slower pace of monthly price increases may lead the CBN to hold rates steady at upcoming Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meetings. Nigeria's inflation rate had previously peaked at 22.97% in May 2025, but has since declined, with the current rate still above desired levels. The CBN's decision on interest rates will be crucial in managing the country's economic challenges.

stories.headline: Inflation could hit 5% next year if Middle East conflict persists
stories.summary: The rate of inflation could reach 5% in 2027 if the conflict in the Middle East continues, severely impacting the global economy. A prolonged war would keep energy prices high, driving up inflation and interest rates, causing difficulties for borrowers. The escalating conflict, particularly in Iran, may trigger a surge in oil prices and disrupt global supply chains, potentially reigniting inflation. As a result, costs of essential items such as food, home energy, and transport are likely to rise. Economists warn that a sustained and prolonged conflict would have far-reaching consequences, affecting the global economy and leading to increased costs for consumers. The potential surge in inflation would be a significant concern, with economists closely monitoring the situation and its impact on the global economy.

stories.headline: Google's open standard for AI agents to discover and verify tools
stories.summary: Google has introduced an open standard for AI agents to discover and verify tools, allowing them to search for and utilize their own tools at runtime. This development is backed by Microsoft and Google, marking a significant advancement in AI capabilities. The new standard enables AI agents to operate more autonomously, finding and using relevant tools as needed. This technology has the potential to enhance various applications, including search and information retrieval. Google has also announced the launch of AI-powered "information agents" that can monitor topics and proactively alert users to updates and changes, further integrating AI into its search features. The open standard is expected to make AI agents more efficient and effective in their operations.

stories.headline: OpenAI chief tells G7 to 'not cede responsibilities' to AI giants
stories.summary: OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman urged G7 leaders to take the lead in regulating artificial intelligence, warning against leaving decisions to the companies developing it. At the G7 summit, Altman emphasized the need for governments to assume responsibility in shaping the technology's future. He predicted that AI models will surpass human capabilities in everything within one to two years, stating that systems with "astonishing power" will be built in the near future. Altman's comments come as Europe expresses concerns about the dominance of US-based AI companies. The call for government regulation highlights the growing importance of AI and the need for international cooperation to address its implications and ensure responsible development. Altman's remarks underscore the rapid progress of AI and the need for proactive governance to mitigate potential risks and maximize benefits.

stories.headline: Microsoft’s China AI Business Grows on OpenAI Model Sales
stories.summary: Microsoft's China AI business is growing due to sales of OpenAI models, despite US-China rivalry over artificial intelligence. ByteDance, a Chinese company, spends $1 billion annually on OpenAI models via Azure, contributing to Microsoft's thriving China AI business. OpenAI's CEO, Sam Altman, acknowledges the AI revolution's staying power. Microsoft is expanding its AI offerings by adding Anthropic's AI models to its Office 365 Copilot suite, reducing reliance on OpenAI. The company is also investing billions in OpenAI, planning to roll out new enterprise services based on generative AI products. This growth underscores Microsoft's significant presence in China's AI market, with the company navigating US export bans to maintain its business relationships with Chinese companies. Microsoft's investments in AI are expected to further drive its growth in the Chinese market.

stories.headline: Google Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer to join IPO-bound OpenAI
stories.summary: Noam Shazeer, a vice president of engineering at Google and co-lead of its Gemini artificial intelligence models, is leaving the company to join OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT. Shazeer, who is also the founder of Character.AI, announced his departure on Wednesday, June 17. The move is seen as part of the intensifying battle among AI companies to secure top talent. OpenAI is reportedly preparing for an initial public offering (IPO). Shazeer's decision to join the company highlights the competition for skilled professionals in the AI sector. His experience in leading Google's Gemini models and founding Character.AI is expected to be an asset to OpenAI as it continues to develop its AI technologies. The move is significant in the context of the ongoing AI talent war among tech companies.

stories.headline: AI Pauses A lot of things are always happening. Only one story matters. Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 were shut down, by the White House, via an imposition of export
stories.summary: The White House imposed export controls on Anthropic's large language models, Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5, resulting in their shutdown. The models were launched just 72 hours prior and were disabled for all users, both inside and outside the US. Anthropic has since announced that it will release Claude Mythos 5 to trusted organizations and a modified version of Claude Fable 5 to the public, which the company claims cannot be used for cyberattacks. The US government directive was issued at 5:23pm on Friday, causing a scramble and disruption to users. The shutdown is a significant development in the regulation of AI models, highlighting the growing concern over their potential misuse. Anthropic's decision to release modified versions of the models aims to balance accessibility with security concerns. The incident marks a notable intervention by the US government in the AI sector.
